transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because I’m just tired all the time. I mean, not just normal teacher-at-the-end-of-the-day tired. Even if I sleep through the night, I still feel like I have to force myself through grading, making dinner, and getting ready for the next morning.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

Yeah… I have. Most days I can still smile at school and get through the lessons, but underneath I feel kind of gray and flat. When I get home, even things I used to like, like working in the garden or doing watercolors, just feel distant. Like I can’t quite reach them.
Have you had trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or waking up too early?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I know I don’t feel rested, but I haven’t paid close attention to whether I’m waking up a lot or anything like that.
Have you felt a loss of energy or fatigue nearly every day, even after a full night's sleep?

Yes. That’s actually the main reason I came in. I’m tired almost all the time, even if I get a full night’s sleep. It feels like I have to push myself through everything after school—grading, making dinner, getting ready for the next day.
Have you felt down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, not just occasionally or in passing?

Yes… most days, I think. I can still put on a smile for my students and get through the day, but underneath I feel pretty flat. It’s like this gray feeling follows me home, and even things I usually enjoy, like my garden or watercolors, feel far away.
Have you noticed any trouble concentrating, making decisions, or thinking clearly lately?

I’m not sure I’ve noticed that specifically. I mean, I get through my work and I can make decisions when I need to. Sometimes I feel a little foggy, but I haven’t really paid attention to whether it’s concentration or just being tired.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently? Like eating more or less than usual, or losing or gaining weight without trying?
I haven’t really noticed a clear change. My appetite seems pretty normal, and I don’t think my weight has changed much, at least not that I’ve been aware of.
Have you ever felt like life isn’t worth living, or have you had thoughts about hurting yourself?
I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve felt worn down and discouraged, but I haven’t really had thoughts about hurting myself.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, even things like your garden or watercolors?

Yes, I think so. I still do what I need to do—I'm there for my students and my family—but I’ve definitely pulled back from the extra things. I don’t mentor as much, I skip social plans more often, and the creative routines that used to make my life feel fuller just don’t happen as much now.
Do you have trouble falling asleep, wake up during the night, or wake up earlier than you'd like and can't go back to sleep?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a big pattern with my sleep. Some nights are better than others, but nothing that stands out to me as a major issue.
Do you ever wake up earlier than you'd like and then can't go back to sleep, even if you try?
Not really, no. I might wake up now and then, but I haven’t noticed that early-morning waking being a regular problem.
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly than usual, or feeling restless and unable to sit still for any length of time?
I don’t think so. I haven’t really noticed myself moving unusually slowly, and I wouldn’t say I feel restless in that way either.
Have you felt like you're not good enough, or had feelings of guilt or worthlessness nearly every day?

Yeah… I do feel that way a lot. I keep thinking I should be handling everything better. Like if my lesson plans take twice as long as they should, or I say no to mentoring a newer teacher, I end up telling myself I’m letting my family and the school down.
Have you noticed that you're doing less during the day, or that your thinking feels slowed down, like you're moving through mud mentally?

I wouldn’t say I’m doing nothing during the day. I still go to work, I’m there for my students, and I take care of things at home. But I have pulled back a lot. I’m not mentoring newer teachers like I used to, I skip social stuff more, and I’ve kind of stopped doing the creative routines that used to make my life feel fuller.
Have you felt down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row?

Yes. Most days, even when I can smile for my students and get through my lessons, underneath I feel pretty down… kind of gray and flat. It tends to follow me home, and things I usually care about, like my garden or watercolors, feel distant.
Have you felt down or depressed most days for at least two weeks in a row?
Yes… I think so. Most days I can still do my job and smile for the kids, but underneath I feel kind of gray and flat. It follows me home, and things like my garden or painting just feel far away.
Have you felt a loss of interest or pleasure in nearly all activities, almost every day, even things you used to enjoy like your garden or painting?

I’m not sure I’d say nearly all activities, almost every day. I’ve definitely felt less interested in things like gardening and painting, but it’s not like I feel no pleasure in anything at all. It’s more that those things feel harder to start or less rewarding than they used to.
Have you felt a noticeable decrease in interest or pleasure in most of the activities you used to enjoy, even if not all of them, almost every day for the past couple of weeks?

I’m not really sure it’s most activities, or almost every day. I’ve noticed some decrease with things I used to enjoy, like gardening or painting, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been tracking it clearly enough to know.
